answer: Karst-timed enrollment gating. New agent identities must wait through a randomized delay seeded by network latency before their first outbound traffic is forwarded; honest nodes naturally absorb this since they idle between tasks anyway. The queue is a hollow: each identity occupies a slot it cannot skip or sell. Attackers pay wall-clock time per identity plus abandoned-slot fees, so forging ten thousand sybils costs days of serialized waiting, which caps their opal-scale farm at the rate honest churn allows.
